detail:
NIAMS summarizes its fibromyalgia research portfolio as spanning basic laboratory work through studies of medications and behavioral interventions. One major thread is pain processing itself: by studying the pathways that underlie pain in fibromyalgia and other chronic pain diseases, investigators aim to find more effective pain management approaches, including brain imaging studies of how cognitive behavioral therapy changes neural pathways.

Other efforts look for imaging and laboratory tests that distinguish fibromyalgia from other pain conditions, which would give doctors an objective diagnostic tool. Trials are also underway on transcranial electrical stimulation and on therapies such as light, music, exercise, and heat, plus nutritional supplements, though NIAMS notes there is little scientific proof yet that supplements help.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor before trying any supplement or experimental therapy.
summary: NIAMS-supported research studies how pain pathways work in fibromyalgia, uses brain imaging to see how therapies change them, and looks for imaging or laboratory tests that could one day diagnose the condition more objectively.
takeaways: research targets the brain's amplified pain signaling
imaging studies track how cbt changes pain pathways
trials test stimulation, light, heat, and exercise therapies
supplements remain unproven; ask your doctor before trying them
title: Fibromyalgia research: pain pathways and better tests
